thread:
Alex Kim: Heads-up — saw flaky streaming disconnects when token refresh retries kick in while an AbortController is cancelling the client. Repro on Node: simple streaming gen -> abort after 2s, sometimes server sees final chunk + duplicate auth call. Reproducer + logs below. cc @Maria Chen @Samir Patel :eyes:

Maria Chen: can you paste the logs? curious if it's fetch vs our retry wrapper.

Alex Kim: logs:
```
[client] 2026-03-01T12:34:56Z start stream req id=abcd
[auth]   2026-03-01T12:34:57Z refresh started
[client] 2026-03-01T12:34:58Z abort signal received
[server] 2026-03-01T12:34:58Z emitted final chunk req id=abcd
[auth]   2026-03-01T12:34:59Z refresh retry (429)
```

Samir Patel: hmm looks like our retry wrapper retries after abort reaches network layer. Node's AbortController cancels fetch but our retry wrapper doesn't short-circuit on abort until after backoff. So refresh fires again. In Python requests we cancel at session level earlier — behaviour differs.

Maria Chen: if we update retry wrapper to check `signal.aborted` before scheduling backoff, that should fix. PR? :+1:

Alex Kim: opened quick PR: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/1287> — adds `if (signal?.aborted) return Promise.reject(new AbortError())` before backoff. Also adjusted streaming teardown to flush KV cache only after abort settled.

Luis Ortega: quick q — does this affect Dedicated clients or only Hosted? I saw it on Dedicated via envoy.

Samir Patel: affects both. Envoy kept the TCP open long enough for server to finish chunk. Need to ensure we don't start auth refresh after abort. I'll review PR tomorrow. @Maria can you add a unit test that simulates abort during retry backoff?

Maria Chen: on it. I'll add tests and a short integration in CI. filing follow-up issue for python parity: #455.

devex-bot: Reminder: add changelog entry and link to 4.1.3 release notes.

Alex Kim: Thanks — will merge after approvals. tl;dr: root cause = retry/backoff not checking abort signal; fix PR + test + python parity ticket.
